newsitem.title: ITALY: Minister says blackout behind Italy botulism case.
newsitem.headline: Minister says blackout behind Italy botulism case.

text.p: Italy's health minister said on Wednesday that an outbreak of botulism this month which killed a teenaged boy had been caused by an electrical failure during production of a batch of mascarpone cheese.

Minister Rosy Bindi told a committee of the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) that there were seven confirmed cases of botulism linked to mascarpone, a soft, sweet dessert cheese, in the southern regions of Campania and Calabria.
Consumer alarm abounded when the botulism scare was revealed when a 15-year-old boy in Naples died on September 7.

Italian health inspectors seized more than 100,000 tubs of mascarpone sold under the Giglio, Parmalat and Sol di Valle brand names and the European Union launched a probe to determine whether Italy had taken necessary steps to safeguard consumers.
"There was an interruption of electricity which did not allow the correct production of mascarpone, encouraging...the development of botulism," Bindi said.
Botulism is a severe form of poisoning from foods that contain a toxin which can affect the central nervous system. In fatal cases, death is often caused by heart and lung failure.
The bacteria is most typically found in improperly preserved canned raw meat.
